RAJA VIJAYARAGHAVAN V, J.
 -------------------------------------
 Crl.M.C No. 3197 of 2023  -------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 12th day of June, 2023  ORDER I have heard Sri. Millu Dandapani, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would point out that in terms of the provisions of Section 42 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Food Analyst, after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer, is required to analyze the sample and send the analysis report mentioning methods of sampling within a period of 14 days to the designated officer with a copy to the Commissioner of Food Safety.

It is further submitted that under Sub-Section 3 of Section 42, the designated officer, after scrutiny of the report of the Food Analyst, is to decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only and in the case of contravention punishable with imprisonment he is required to submit recommendation within 14 days to the Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning the prosecution.

The learned counsel submits that in the case on hand, the prosecution sanction order was issued from the office of the Commissioner of Food Safety only on 11.08.2020, though the report issued by the Food Analyst was on 05.03.2020.
Reliance is placed on the order rendered by the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court to bolster his contention that the delay is fatal and the proceedings are liable to be quashed.
Having regard to the submissions advanced, further proceedings in ST No.1357/2020 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Angamaly will stand stayed for a period of six weeks.
